q:
we sleep trained at 5.5 months with modified Ferber. it went very well and LO took to it so well she started to drop to 2 naps around 6 monfhs 

shes now 7 months & everything went to shit 1 week ago when we were out of town visiting family.
x: Parent of a 7-month-old whose training held until a family trip.

q: for about 1 week prior to travel we had pulled back to a 3.25 last WW due to more false starts (yay) and it worked like a charm. she was sleeping 11-11.5 hours straight through, zero issues.
x: Same parent: the last schedule fix had held about a week before the trip.

q: my intention was to re-Ferber but she doesn’t need it for sleep onset; she needs it for false starts and it. just. does. not. work.
x: Same parent on why retraining the old way fails this time.

q: im desperate and drowning and feel totally trapped! please help!!
x: Same parent closing the post.

q: I was so nervous that pushing WW back to 3.5+ would make things worse because that’s part of how we got in a false start rut in the first place! I just couldn’t figure out if she had a sleep debt from all the broken nights or was under tired CAUSING broke nights!
x: Same parent replying to a commenter's longer wake windows.

q: Because going back to our original wake windows did indeed help! However even on 3.25/3.25/3.5-3.75 she has woken up at 10 pm screaming & requiring intervention. And we still had an EMW at 5:35 this morning after 3 days without one.
x: Same parent four days later: the commenter's fix helped, then slipped.

q: She did 3.25/3.25/3.5 for a couple of days and nights were great save for a little cry at 10, 12, and 4 but she went back to sleep just fine. I’ll definitely try pushing a little more!
x: Same parent the same day, on the couple of good nights.

q:
Well, I decided to do it cold turkey. She does really good about it for her naps. Bedtime absolutely SUCKS. This is the second night. 

I’ve been fighting with her for almost 3 hours now.
x: Parent of a 2-year-old on night 2 of taking the dummy away.

q: Do I just keep letting her cry? How long is too long? Do I go in and rub her back until she falls asleep again? Will that start another habit?
x: Same parent's exact questions.

q: I’m definitely going to stand my ground and not give it back. I have a really hard time persevering. It feels like it’ll be like this forever, which is ridiculous to say since it’s only night 2.
x: Same parent after a commenter's encouragement.

q: How long is too long to let her cry? I truly thought she would’ve given up and just laid down by a certain point.
x: Same parent's version of the post in another sub.

q: My 10.5 month old has been teething for over 3 weeks now and waking 4-8 times a night.
x: Parent of a teething 10.5-month-old fed back to sleep at each waking.

q: Since 6 weeks old he used to give me 7 hour stretches, waking 1-2 times overnight to feed. Now he does a 4 hour stretch, then wakes up every 1-1.5 hours. He’s never accepted a pacifier so I’m always up rocking or feeding him back to sleep. This change has shattered me.
x: Parent of a 4-month-old since the swaddle stopped.

q: Update: day 3 and sleep training worked […] I feel very guilty. I had barely slept for 2 months with no help during the day while his dad was at work, I was struggling.
x: Same parent a week later: training worked by day 3 but the guilt stayed.

q: Although I’m drenched in guilt, I feel like I did the right thing for him?
x: Same parent ending the update.

q: Currently working on getting her to sleep more independently using pick up put down.
x: Parent of a 7-month-old logging a pick-up-put-down night.

q: Then slept for 2hrs to 3:30, had a feed, down at 4, up at 5, down again at 5:15 and I'm typing this at 5:50.
x: Same parent writing before dawn.

q: I tried again that evening and it was hell it’s like he knew and was hysterical so we gave up after 20 minutes as he was crying so much he was sick.
x: Breastfeeding mother of a 5-month-old on a gentle Ferber attempt.

q: please does anyone have any tips or methods to try. should i try ferber again?? i am desperate.
x: Same mother's ask.

q: I feel that is impossible for him at this stage those wake windows are a struggle for him already some days that your example would be impossible as he would be extremely fussy and overtired.
x: Same mother rejects a commenter's longer wake windows.

q: Yes I was relying on chatGPT too but clearly it was wrong
x: Same mother a day later on where her schedule came from.

q: So we did CIO, which was working for 4 nights. On the 5th night he was crying more and more so I gave in and rocked him. Now we are back to MOTN wake ups lasting hours again.
x: Mother of a 7-month-old: CIO worked four nights, then she stopped.

q: We didn’t think ferber would work bc every time we go in the room our baby he’s more hysterical.
x: Same mother on choosing CIO.

q: We felt bad bc during the day our baby has been way more clingy and won’t let us set him down without crying which is not his usual personality. Idk if this is bc we made him CIO.
x: Same mother on the guilt after stopping.

q: My wife and I did the whole thing—read the books, watched the YouTubers, took the classes. We knew babies eat every 2-3 hours. We thought we were prepared. We weren't. Not even close.
x: Father one month in, on preparation that did not help.

q: The 3 AM feeding is the worst. You finally get them down, you crawl back into bed, your head hits the pillow... and 45 minutes later, the screaming starts again. Your heart just drops.
x: Same father on the 3am feed.

q: Is there an actual hack to make the night routine faster? I’m desperate for some proof that I’ll eventually feel like a human being again.
x: Same father's ask, after snapping at his wife.

q: She is in daycare so nap is outside of our control
x: Parent of a just-turned-2-year-old waking for 3.5 weeks.

q: Is this just what the 2 year regression is?! How long does it last? She already sleeps so much less than other kids so I don’t know what to even do now. Capping nap isn’t an option
x: Same parent's ask.

q: She will not go back to sleep until I go in her room and sit next to her while she falls asleep. Once a night? Fine I can do that. 5 times a night?? I’m exhausted.
x: Mother of a 3-year-old who used to sleep 12 hours, after an overseas move.

q: she doesn’t want her dad to do anything for her, she always says “no, just mama”.
x: Same mother: the father, newly back, cannot help.

q: she was an absolute dream baby for the first 5 weeks but things have gotten ROUGH recently.
x: Breastfeeding first-time mother of a 7-week-old unsettled by day.

q: thankfully we have a wonderful village and wishing 20 minutes of sending up the smoke signal for help i had a house full of people to support me and baby.
x: Same mother on family arriving the day she struggled alone.

q: My 11 month old has been a terrible sleeper from the beginning. She wakes up every 2-3 hours and has since she was a newborn. Overnight is miserable. I can barely function to do my job and I feel like my mental health is really being affected.
x: Nursing mother of an 11-month-old who has never slept long.

q: Daycare has always said she’s not a good napper.
x: Same mother on daycare's verdict.

q: I have tried different nap schedules on the weekends and they make no difference. […] I have also changed bedtime between 6:30 and 8 and again makes zero difference.
x: Same mother on schedule changes that did nothing.

q: I’ve tried pick up put down. She screams when I put her down. Tried having husband go in and she wants nothing to do with it
x: Same mother on methods tried.

q: I’m writing this at 4am, but last night I rocked her to sleep at 6:50 pm. First wake up at 7:30, rocked back to sleep. Second wakeup 9pm and fed her because she wouldn’t go back down.
x: Same mother's night log.

q: I can deal with lack of sleep but this is on another level. Even if I could get to 2 nighttime awakenings I would be happy. Any thoughts are appreciated. I don’t feel CIO a good option because she will literally work herself up to the point of actual screaming and sobbing inconsolably.
x: Same mother's modest goal and her limit.

q: I’d really love to hear from people who had babies that strongly refused bottles and/or the bassinet/cot for a period of time - not just babies who took to it with a few tweaks.
x: Breastfeeding mother of a 7-week-old who only sleeps in the carrier.

q: I think a lot of the usual tips are geared towards babies who were already somewhat open to bottles or sleeping independently, and that just doesn’t seem to be my baby.
x: Same mother on why common tips miss.

q: I'm in a local mums group and it felt like only my baby was doing this but probably I need to step away from that. Everyone in that groups baby's sleep in the bassinet and cot
x: Same mother on her local mothers' group.

q: We stared Ferber last night and he cried for 30 mins at bedtime and then fell asleep. He slept for a beautiful 8h30min stretch (7:55pm-4:23am). We were ecstatic.
x: Parent of a 6-month-old after Ferber night one.

q: He fell asleep in my arms within 10 mins of me picking him up. Did we ruin the whole thing? I know that assisting after crying can only reinforce the crying and confuse him, I’m feeling so defeated.
x: Same parent after picking up at 5:30am.

q: Should I had continue to let him cry? How should we handle wakes in the second half of the night when sleep pressure is low? Please advise!
x: Same parent's ask.

q: I’m looking at doing a modified Ferber.. I’m just scared to start trying. I know that once you start you need to commit until they get it and I don’t know if my heart can take it
x: Mother of an 8-month-old who can no longer rock her to sleep.

q: I don’t want her to think no one is coming for her and just give up and go to sleep…like I know she needs to learn to fall asleep on her own but I don’t want it to be because she’s given up on calling me.
x: Same mother on her fear about crying methods.

q: TLDR: just need some encouragement on how to ferberize my baby esp with her standing and how do I not feel like an awful mom and like I’m making her cry herself to sleep???
x: Same mother's ask.

q: Previously we were letting her cry until she went back to sleep but now that she’s sick and congested, I’m not sure that’s the best course of action. So I’ve been more responsive but honestly, it doesn’t work.
x: Parent of a sick 7-month-old trained with crying.

q: it feels wrong to let her cry when she’s sick? What am I supposed to do? We’ve been starting our day at 4:30/5am lately while she’s been sick and it’s been miserable.
x: Same parent on early mornings during the illness.

q: He slept SO good through the night for about a month and then the regression happened at 4 months. His sleep is getting increasingly worse. First he was waking up once, then twice, now he wakes up every 45 minutes for the first 3 hours and then every 2-3 hours after that.
x: Parent of a 5-month-old bottle-fed back to sleep.

q: I don’t even need him to sleep all the way through the night, just sleep more. Please help. We are so exhausted.
x: Same parent's cross-post adds a modest goal.

q: We had tried the Phillips Avent Soothie, Ninni Co, and Bibs original. With all of these she just will suck for a few seconds (that if she actually takes it) and then spit it out, and it never works to help soothe her or get her to sleep.
x: Breastfeeding parent of a 6-week-old on three dummies tried.

q: Is she just not a pacifier baby, or should we keep getting different ones to try?
x: Same parent's ask.

q: She has been sleep trained for nights for nearly 2 months, but it’s been a fairly rocky road. She still cries every night on average 5-10 min, but has a random 30 minute night of crying about once per week. Once she’s asleep, she does great for the rest of the night with just one feed then right back to sleep, so we’ve just accepted the crying at bedtime for what it is.
x: Parent of a 6-month-old two months after night training.

q: I tried the gentle nap training suggested in the mod post for 4 days and she cried all 15 minutes, then I would rescue with a contact nap. I am thinking we’re going to have to do CIO and leave her for an hour and just hope and pray she falls asleep.
x: Same parent on nap training so far.

q: Her pediatrician thinks she’s still crying at night bc I’m doing all contact naps during the day and confusing her.
x: Same parent quotes the paediatrician.
